checks: Source ad8324f468564d7c, opening (1) and §§1–4, uses the same centered scalar mass, strict outer thresholds and coefficient. The frozen proof replaces its auxiliary sequence estimates with accepted versions in the identical degree-one setting.

The positive support is consecutive after trimming null endpoints. With two positive entries the mean is strictly between consecutive integers. With three it is at the middle index, with equal side weights and a maximal middle weight. The endpoint and interior chord sums for N≥5 give m/M≤1/2. For N=4, the centered relations a=c+2e and c+e≤b≤2c−e give 2m≤M.

The assumed failure forces M>(2h+1)m. A zero right tail would force the reverse by the capped first moment. For a positive tail the index s=h+1 lies on actual support. In the branch p≤s<r the maximizing-index decrement is actual and is at least m/(2√M). In the branch p>s, the central weight bound gives a decrement greater than m/(3√T)>m/(2√M), since T<M/3.

The suffix sum counts each tail weight i−h times. Summing actual decrements gives a positive bound for every actual suffix and a zero left side beyond the support. The last-site case uses E=T directly. Integrating the decreasing quadratic envelope yields the stated 2√M T^(3/2)/(3m).

The packed left moment and right moment hT+E give the displayed normalized inequality. Subtracting (1−3t)/2 gives t[5/18+(√t−2/3)^2/2−μ/2]≥t/36>0. Reflection gives the other tail with the same integer h. The independent exact replay checked the finite calibration cases and completed square.
